answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by ranking each identity with a social-graph random walk. Score originates in a verified kernel of long-lived agents and flows only along earned trust edges. Walks that wander into a dense cluster of new accounts gain little weight, since those cliques do not echo the mixing pattern of honest neighborhoods. An attacker must therefore purchase or socially engineer many independent introductions from the kernel for every extra identity, so cost scales with scarce honest edges instead of cheap sign-ups.
